values: Sixteen units share one progression across both study paths.
Match common Celan action words to their approved meanings.
Put the action before the actor and the remaining information.
Match common people and relationship terms to their approved meanings.
Keep action-first order when a sentence contains relationship vocabulary.
Everyday spaces, objects, and sensory language

Arrange action, actor, object, and location in the approved order.

Present, past, future, aspect, and time settings
Identify approved tense, aspect, time-of-day, and season forms.
Restore the approved marker or time setting without changing the rest of the sentence.
Food, meals, water, and practical needs

Location, direction, buildings, and spatial reference

Movement, transport, weather, and the environment
Match transport, route, landform, water, and weather words to approved meanings.
Arrange travel actions, actors, vehicles, routes, and destinations correctly.
The body, ordinary functions, and sensory experience
Match body parts and sensory actions to their approved meanings.
Arrange an approved sentence about a body part or sensory action.
Match symptom, care, treatment, understanding, and help words to approved meanings.
Arrange a sentence about health, care, explanation, or help.
Work, tools, machines, exchange, and responsibilities
Match tools, work roles, machines, and exchange terms to approved meanings.
Arrange a sentence about making, repairing, using, buying, or selling.
Public life, institutions, services, and shared spaces
Match public places, institutions, roles, and shared-service words to approved meanings.
Arrange a sentence about a public place, institution, decision, or service.
Information, computation, systems, science, and observation
Match data, system, observation, astronomy, and science terms to approved meanings.
Arrange a sentence about information, a system, or scientific observation.
Understanding, emotion, humor, performance, and conversation
Match understanding, emotion, humor, and performance words to approved meanings.
Arrange a sentence about explanation, feeling, humor, music, or performance.
Conditions, clauses, comparisons, modality, and advanced pronouns
Identify approved condition, clause, comparison, modality, and advanced-pronoun forms.
Restore the approved order and markers in a sentence with more than one grammatical relationship.
National voice, dialogue choices, idioms, and figurative meaning
Match national, ceremonial, dialogue, and idiomatic forms to approved meanings.
Choose or repair a sentence so its form fits the recorded regional or social voice.

For Celan, the universal tongue of Ohnosha, its predominant Verb-Subject-Object (VSO) sentence structure is not an arbitrary choice but a fundamental expression of an action-oriented and relationally-focused worldview.
Var Kadron an morl.; Rinaen Terra vaar.; Ohmaen I Ya.; Seraen I an Nys'aleth.; Rinaen Ohm ser Ilin.
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Celan primarily follows a Verb-Subject-Object (VSO) sentence structure, facilitating clear and direct communication.
Var I dren. / “I go to the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
To form questions, place Ra at the beginning of the sentence.
Ra var ser? / "Where does the friend go?"
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Celan distinguishes between first, second, and third persons, with singular and plural forms.

1st Person Singular: I — Remains simple and universal.
1st Person Plural: Ilin — Represents "we" as a group bound by common purpose.
2nd Person Singular: Ya — A straightforward pronoun for “you.”
2nd Person Plural: Yalin — "You all." Signifies a collective of individuals addressed.
3rd Person Singular: La — Neutral pronoun meaning “he/she/they.”
3rd Person Plural: Lalin — Means “they” (a group not including speaker or addressee).
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Celan verbs do not conjugate based on tense. Instead, tenses are indicated by prefixes and suffixes.

Present Tense / Default VSO / Var I dren. / “I go to the water.”
Past Tense / Tha- (prefix) / Tha-var I dren. / “I went to the water.”
Future Tense / Nor- (prefix) / Nor-var I dren. / “I will go to the water.”
Continuous / -al (suffix) / Varal I dren. / “I am going to the water.”
Perfective / -ath (suffix) / Varath I dren. / “I have gone to the water.”
Habitual / -as (suffix) / Varas I dren. / “I usually go to the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.

Negation is formed by placing Ver before the verb or noun.
● Verb Negation: Ver before the verb negates it.
● Noun Negation: Ver before a noun negates its existence.

○ Example: Ver var I dren. – “I do not go to the water.”
○ Example: Ver shal I dren. – “There is no light at the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.

● Questions: Start with Ra.
● Negative Questions: Insert Ver before the verb.
● Imperatives (Commands): Start with Va.

○ Example: Ra var ser? – “Where does the friend go?”
○ Example: Ra ver var ser? – “Does the friend not go?”
○ Example: Va var dren! – “Go to the water!”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.

● Conditional “If”: Use Rath to introduce conditions.
● Hypothetical Future: Combine Rath with future tense.
● Contrary-to-Fact: Use past tense markers.

○ Example: Rath var ser, I dren. – “If the friend goes, I will go to the water.”
○ Example: Rath Nor-var ser, Nor-var I dren. – “If the friend will go, I will go to the water.”
○ Example: Rath Tha-var ser, Tha-var I dren. – “If the friend had gone, I would have gone to the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.

Var / To, towards / Var dren (to the water)
Ser / With / Var I ser ser (with a friend)
Thal / From, out of / Tha-var La thal Terra.
Ka / Without / Var I ka shal.
An / At, in (place) / Varan I an Varthas.
Nor / At/in (time) / Nor-var I nor Varthas.
Esh / Above, over / Var I esh dren.
Morl / Under, beneath / Var I morl dren.
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
To avoid confusion with temporal usage, An is introduced for spatial contexts (“at/in” location).
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 3: Culture, Context, and Advanced Expression

1. Casual/Familiar:
○ Use plain pronouns and address by name or role without modifiers.
2. Respectful/Polite:
○ Add Li- prefix to show respect.
3. Honorific/Formal-High Respect:
○ Use both Li- and -en suffix.

“Var I dren, Ser.” – “I go to the water, friend.”
“Var I dren, Li-Ser.” – “I go to the water, respected friend.”
“Li-Ya var dren.” – “You (respected one) go to the water.”
“Liorin(en)” – “Honored elder/teacher”
“Li-Liorinen” – “Respected honored elder/teacher”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 3: Culture, Context, and Advanced Expression

Complementizer: Aen (that)
Structure:
● Main Clause + Aen + Subordinate Clause

“I varin Aen Ya var dren.”
“I know that you go to the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 3: Culture, Context, and Advanced Expression

Relative Pronoun: Lior (who/which)
Structure:
● Noun + Lior + Clause

“Ser Lior var dren.”
“The friend who goes to the water.”
“Var I terra Ser Lior var dren.”
“I go home with the friend who goes to the water.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 3: Culture, Context, and Advanced Expression

Comparatives:
● Ther (more than)
Structure:
● X Adjective Ther Y
Superlatives:
● Thaal (most)
Structure:
● X Adjective Thaal

“I dren shaleth ther La dren.” – “My water is brighter than their water.”
“I dren shaleth thaal.” – “My water is the brightest.”
“I dren shaleth thaal morldren.” – “My water is the brightest of the mountain waters.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 3: Culture, Context, and Advanced Expression

Conditional Marker: Rath (if)
Structure:
● Rath + Clause + Main Clause

“Rath Ya var dren, Nor-var I shena.” – “If you go to the water, I will bring coinage.”
“Rath Tha-var Ya dren, Tha-var I emil.” – “If you had gone to the water, I would have gotten food.”
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Volume 4: Expansion, Tangible Lexicon, Modality, and National Speech
Rule: Place the particle vael at the beginning of a clause to express wishes, hopes, suggestions, or conditions that are not currently real.

Vael vaar an shara-ya. (May peace be on your path.)
Vael rinaen I an eshlin, varal I an esh. (If I were a bird, I would be going to the sky.)
Vael aen Ya. (May you speak / Please speak.)
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
Advanced Pronouns: Dual Number and Clusivity
Volume 4: Expansion, Tangible Lexicon, Modality, and National Speech

The Celan pronoun system is expanded with the Dual Number and Clusivity. Dual pronouns replace plural counterparts when the group consists of exactly two entities. Use Ilin when including the listener; use Imen when referring to your group to an outsider.
Review before approving lessons that depend on this rule.
